name: What an AI shopping assistant can do on a shop's own pages
buyer: Online shops that want to know where a machine reading their pages gives up, and anybody wondering what we would ever publish about a named shop
cadence: opt-in only, no shop on the table yet
cadence_long: One published reading of what a machine that only reads pages can do, re-checked against the lane's own sealed document on every build
who: Online shops that want to know where a machine reading their pages gives up, and anybody wondering what we would ever publish about a shop that did not ask.
note: BORN NOT FOR SALE 2026-08-25. The Agent-Ready Table is a public comparison table: one row per online shop, saying how far a machine that only READS pages gets on that shop's own product pages, and what that shop's own robots file says about the named shopping assistants. NOBODY IS ON IT, and that is not a build failure -- it is the lane refusing itself. Two separate written permissions have to be in place before one name can appear and only one of them is. The operator's dated decision at revenue-2026/approvals/read_public_sites.md reads `status: ACTIVE`, `approved_on: 2026-08-25`, and it answers ONE question: may a machine of ours read other companies' public websites at all. It does not answer the second question a table about named businesses cannot publish without -- WHO IS ON THE TABLE, and where that list of names came from. The lane's own written declaration at revenue-2026/projects/agent_ready/rules/shop-list-source.json, `written_on: 2026-08-25`, reads `terms_status: NOT_READ` and names nobody, so engine/sources.list_source() answers unknown, the lane fetches nothing, and the table has no rows. OPERATOR DECISION NEEDED: which shop list, and somebody reading that source's terms on a named day and writing down what they said. Nothing in this build may write that declaration, because a machine that can declare its own list source has no list source. NO SHOP, NO PERSON AND NO PRICE IS NAMED ANYWHERE ON THE PAGE. Nothing has ever been sold here: the lane's sales table holds no rows, read read-only as the page was built, and the catalog price stays 'Not for sale yet'. The lane's code carries two prices for the paid evidence report and neither is printed on this page, because a price on the page is a promise this build has no authority to make. WHAT THE PAGE PRINTS IS THE LANE'S OWN PUBLISHED DOCUMENT, WORD FOR WORD, NOT A DESCRIPTION OF IT: revenue-2026/var/agent_ready_data.db holds one render, state `published`, `on_day: 2026-08-25`, and scripts/slice_agent_ready.py RE-CHECKS THAT DOCUMENT'S FINGERPRINT with the lane's own hashing function before printing a character of it -- a document whose stored fingerprint no longer matches its stored text stops the build. Every date on the page is read off a dated row or a dated file in that way; not one is taken from this machine's clock, which reads two different days depending on the setting. SAMPLE STATUS IS on-page AND IT IS ENFORCED, NOT ASSERTED: every table in the lane's store is empty except the one holding that published document, so there is no file to sample and the page IS the whole of what we hold. The slicer reads the store read-only on every build and REFUSES TO BUILD if a row appears in any table other than the renders table, because 'the whole of what we hold is printed on this page' stops being true the moment a shop is listed. THE LANE'S OWN WORDING GUARD IS RUN AGAIN AT PAGE-BUILD TIME AND IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: the published document must clear projects/agent_ready/row.wording_problems(), and a line assembled out of that guard's own first banned phrase must be refused -- a guard nobody has seen say no is a decoration. THE PAGE CANNOT REACH THE NETWORK AND IS PROVED NOT TO ON EVERY BUILD: the lane ships with `FETCHER = None`, the slicer reads that default straight out of the lane's source without running it and refuses to build if it is no longer None, and the slicer never calls the lane's fetch path at all. NO FRESHNESS ROW IS ADDED to scripts/family_status.py, deliberately: the only table in the store with a dated row in it records our own act of publishing, not data about the world, and a freshness tag pointed at it would let a job that ran look exactly like data that moved. The board therefore shows this family as NOT WIRED UP, which is the same honest answer it already gives for free-time and verified-record.
